subject: Renewal: Capacity expansion & tokens/sec commitment for EdgeScale
messages:
From: Joe Park <joe@edgescale.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lara Nguyen <lara@edgescale.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning & target throughput needs

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re finalizing our budget for H2 and want to include a committed expansion on the Redwood Dedicated pool at renewal. Current summary: we need a sustained increase (production load) to support an anticipated 3x growth in generation volume by Q4. Rough target metrics: additional ~40 A100-class GPUs, and a tokens/sec commitment that lets our product maintain 98% of requests under a 400ms generation tail.

Can you share what a recommended reserved-pool commit looks like (tokens/sec) and how Redwood measures that metric? Also, any standard fallback/overage protection you advise if we hit bursts?

Joe
VP Product, EdgeScale
--
Attachments: 20270610-edgescale-draft-ma-schedule.pdf (PDF, 90KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Joe Park <joe@edgescale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning & target throughput needs

Joe —

Appreciate the clarity. High-level first pass below and I’ll follow with a draft addendum you can share with procurement: 

- Recommended commit: baseline reserved pool sized to support 1,200,000 tokens/sec (aggregate across your dedicated pool) with a 10% per-minute burst allowance up to 1,320,000 tokens/sec. We size GPU count (40 A100-equivalents) to meet that steady-state throughput for your typical prompt lengths.
- Measurement: tokens/sec is measured at Redwood’s ingress gateway and calculated as a 1-minute rolling mean; availability SLO is evaluated on the 99th percentile of 1-minute windows during your contracted regional business hours (Mon–Fri 00:00–23:59 PT by default unless you specify otherwise).
- Fallbacks: automated fallback to a compatible quantized model variant (same correctness band) if latency SLOs are at risk, plus cross-region overflow to our secondary us-west2 pool as emergency capacity.
- Credits: for breaches beyond the SLO we propose a time-weighted credit formula (draft language below).

I’ll attach a measurement-spec workbook and a redlineable addendum by EOD Friday. If you want different working hours or stricter P99 thresholds, tell me and we’ll adjust.

-Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Joe Park <joe@edgescale.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Renewal appendix — tokens/sec guarantee & SLO language (preview)

Joe & team —

Attached is the draft measurement spec (xlsx) and a preview of the appendix we intend to include with the renewal: a short summary here to make review faster. Please treat as a starting point — procurement/legal we understand will propose edits.

Key clauses preview: 
1) Definitions: 
   - "Committed Throughput" = 1,200,000 tokens/sec (aggregate)
   - "Burst Allowance" = 10% per 60-second interval (measured as peak 1-minute mean)
   - "Measurement Point" = Redwood Ingress Gateway (ingestion point entering the dedicated pool)
2) SLOs & Measurement Windows: 
   - Availability SLO: 99.9% of 1-minute windows per calendar month, measured on the 1-minute rolling mean.
   - Latency SLO: 95% of requests completed under 500ms tail latency for production model v2.1
3) Remedies:
   - Credits computed as (DowntimeMinutes / TotalMinutesInMonth) * MonthlyReservedFee * 0.50
   - If sustained shortfall > 30 minutes in aggregate per month we escalate to an action plan with provisioning of pre-warmed burst capacity free of charge until remediation.
4) Operational controls:
   - Canary window for scale-ups (48 hours) to validate model variant, KV pre-warm, and batching params.
   - Real-time per-route dashboards and token-level billing exported to your SIEM.

Two asks: 1) confirm if 1,200,000 tokens/sec aligns with your internal projections; 2) confirm whether you need the SLO measured at 95th or 99th percentile for the latency metric.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Marissa
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: 20270618-tokensps-measurement-spec.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)
From: Lara Nguyen <lara@edgescale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Joe Park <joe@edgescale.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@edgescale.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Renewal appendix — tokens/sec guarantee & SLO language (preview)

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick draft. A few clarifying questions from Procurement & Ops: 
1) Measurement point — will Redwood provide a sample of raw 1-minute windows (CSV) each day for audit?
2) Credits formula — can we get a cap on total credits per month (we’d prefer an explicit cap rather than open-ended liability)?
3) Burst behavior — can EdgeScale reserve a portion of the burst allowance (e.g., 5% guaranteed burst earmark) so other tenants can’t consume it during scheduled traffic spikes?

We’re okay with the proposed committed throughput if we can agree the above items.

Lara
Head of Ops, EdgeScale
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Nguyen <lara@edgescale.com>, Joe Park <joe@edgescale.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Renewal appendix — tokens/sec guarantee & SLO language (preview)

Lara —

Short answers: 
1) Audit CSVs — yes, we can export daily 1-minute window samples for the prior 30 days to a customer-specified S3/GCS bucket; we’ll include an example file format in the addendum.
2) Credits cap — we can add a cap equal to 50% of the Monthly Reserved Fee; also proposing an optional escalation path (service credits + prioritized remediation) above that for material outages.
3) Burst earmark — we can support a named-burst pool (up to 5% of the committed throughput) reserved for EdgeScale during scheduled events; it will be charged as part of the reserved commitment and not offered to other tenants while active.

Additional notes: measurement uses 1-minute rolling mean at ingress; we also publish P95 & P99 latency histograms. If you want stricter business-hours SLOs or additional reserved burst percentage, we’ll size the pool accordingly and reflect in pricing.

We’ll incorporate these edits into the rev1 addendum. Expect the redline in DocuSign by Monday.

Best,
Laura
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Procurement Team <procurement@edgescale.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Capacity expansion & tokens/sec commitment for EdgeScale — acceptance pending DocuSign

Rishi/Laura/Marissa —

Thanks — we reviewed the rev1 preview and confirm EdgeScale is prepared to proceed on the following items pending DocuSign: 
- Committed Throughput: 1,200,000 tokens/sec (aggregate)
- Reserved burst earmark: 5% (named burst pool)
- Credits cap: 50% Monthly Reserved Fee
- Audit exports to our S3 bucket (example path to follow)

We expect to sign the addendum and the renewed reserved pool order once we receive the DocuSign link and internal approval. Please send the DocuSign to procurement@edgescale.com

Regards,
EdgeScale Procurement
